reason: E2 directly shows edge dislocations govern strength in NbTaTiV and CrMoNbV, supporting the first premise. However, the cited evidence does not address the comparative lattice friction of edge vs. screw dislocations, the temperature sensitivity of edge-dislocation-controlled strength, or the dislocation character of conventional BCC alloys; these premises lack specific support from E1 or E2.
premises: Edge dislocations dominate plasticity in refractory BCC HEAs like NbTaTiV
Edge dislocations create higher lattice friction than screw dislocations
Higher lattice friction from edge dislocations enhances hardness and strength
Edge-dislocation-controlled strength is less temperature-sensitive, yielding a plateau up to ~1073 K
Conventional BCC alloys are screw-dislocation-dominated and thus weaker
